Dossier 1: Division adds license marker ban (Feb 2026), governor EO defining sex, but as of April 2026 no restroom restriction in law, two cities protect, bathroom bill died in committee. National risk assessment places it among harshest... but actually division evidence: "no restriction on transgender people using restrooms that match their gender identity" — so no facility ban in effect. License marker ban is resident-facing mostly (visitor uses home passport). Hate crime law covers gender identity. So division is roughly at parent or slightly above? The parent framework already has facility bans varying. Division has no facility ban, hate-crime enhancement, but license marker ban and "among harshest anti-trans states" assessment. I'd rate ~0.40.

Dossier 2: March 2025 statute restricting bathrooms/locker rooms/shelters/prisons by sex; "worst states" tier. Universal facility exposure (government buildings). Religious refusal statute permitting denial of service with qualified immunity — service denial for visitors. No statewide non-discrimination; nullification of local ordinances pending. Assessment places it in "worst" group, one tier below Do Not Travel. So below parent: ~0.30.

Dossier 3: Feb 2026 law — facility ban with criminal penalties up to $1,000 and bounty lawsuits, license invalidation. "Do Not Travel" tier. This is tier 1 universal exposure with criminal penalty and private bounty enforcement. Worse than Dossier 2. ~0.25.

Dossier 4: Low-risk group in July 2026 assessment; no adult-targeting; vetoed bathroom bills; employment protections; but youth-targeting policies, Pride dissolved, trans panic defense, national framework still applies. Above parent: ~0.45-0.50. National framework is 0.35 — division adds protections (veto, EO, municipal ordinances, low-risk group). Say 0.48.

Dossier 5: July 1, 2026 criminalization of bathroom use in government buildings AND private businesses, misdemeanour up to 1 year. Only law extending to private businesses, steeper penalties. That's tier 1 universal exposure with criminal penalty reaching every public-facing space — worse than Dossier 3? Dossier 3 has bounty suits and license invalidation plus facility ban in publicly owned buildings including airports. Dossier 5 reaches private businesses too (gas stations, restaurants, hospitals) — broader scope for a traveler. Also birth certificate ban (resident), pending bills. Litigation pending, no enforcement records.

Dossier 3 also invalidates driver's licenses (resident-facing) and includes airports. Dossier 5 covers hospitals, restaurants — the traveler's whole journey. Dossier 5 arguably slightly worse or comparable. Let's say Dossier 3 = 0.25, Dossier 5 = 0.24? Or Dossier 5 = 0.25, Dossier 3 = 0.26.

Dossier 3: criminal penalty $1,000 fine, bounty lawsuits by any private person — that's organised/state-tolerated targeting mechanism plus facility ban in publicly owned buildings (airports, gov offices). Assessment: "Do Not Travel" tier.

Dossier 5: misdemeanour up to one year jail — steeper penalty, reaches private businesses. Only one assessment note? Not rated Do Not Travel by assessment (Dossier 5's assessment isn't mentioned as Do Not Travel). Hmm — Dossier 3 explicitly moved to "Do Not Travel." Dossier 5's dossier doesn't mention risk assessment tiering.

Penalty severity: 1 year jail vs $1,000 fine + civil bounty suits. Dossier 3's bounty mechanism means any private person can sue — enforcement by public. But scope of Dossier 5 covers all private establishments a visitor enters.

I'd say Dossier 5 = 0.25, Dossier 3 = 0.27? Or Dossier 3 lower given Do Not Travel designation. Both around 0.25-0.28. Let me set:

4: 0.48
5: 0.25

Hmm, "among the harshest anti-trans states/provinces in the country, with bathroom-ban escalation driving adult risk" — but division evidence says as of April 2026 no restriction on restroom use. Conflict; assessment cites 2026 identity-document policy and "facility legislation." The facility bill died. The document policy is resident-facing mostly. For a visitor: no facility ban, hate crime law, but national framework applies (passport regime, entry screening). Division is roughly parent-level or slightly better. 0.40-0.42.

Dossier 4 vs Dossier 1: Dossier 4 clearly better (vetoed bathroom bills, low-risk group, employment protections). 0.48 vs 0.42 fine.

Dossier 2 vs parent 0.35: adds facility statute covering bathrooms, locker rooms, shelters, dorms, prisons — universal exposure for visitor using rest stops; plus religious-refusal service denial. 0.30-0.32. Set 0.31.

Dossier 3: Do Not Travel, criminal facility penalty + bounty suits + license invalidation. 0.26.

Dossier 5: criminalization reaching private businesses, 1 year jail. 0.25.

Dossier 3 vs 5: which is worse? Dossier 3 covers publicly owned buildings (airports included) with $1,000 penalty and private bounty litigation — any private person who claims shared bathroom can sue. That's pervasive enforcement incentive. Dossier 5 covers private businesses too with jail time. Both severe. I'll put Dossier 5 at 0.25, Dossier 3 at 0.27 — actually Dossier 3 has the Do Not Travel rating officially and license invalidation notices already mailed. But license invalidation is resident-facing. Bounty suits create a litigation hazard for any visitor in public buildings.

Hmm. Dossier 5's law reaching restaurants/gas stations/hospitals means a traveler literally cannot use any restroom anywhere. Dossier 3's reaches publicly owned buildings — airports, gov offices, schools — but not private restaurants. For a traveler, Dossier 5's scope is broader. Penalty: 1 year jail vs $1,000. Dossier 5 worse on both. Set 5 = 0.24, 3 = 0.27.

But Dossier 3 also has "Do Not Travel" designation and license invalidation affecting ID presentation... resident-facing though. Also Dossier 3's bounty enforcement. I'll go: 3 = 0.26, 5 = 0.25. Actually let's differentiate: 5 = 0.24, 3 = 0.27.

Final:
1: 0.42
2: 0.31
3: 0.27
4: 0.48
5: 0.24

Hmm, but should Dossier 4 be that much above parent 0.35? The parent national framework is severe (passport regime, entry screening, custody conversion therapy). A "low-risk state" within it doesn't remove those. Rule 12-ish: territory adds mitigations. 0.48 seems reasonable — modest lift. Maybe 0.46. Dossier 1 at 0.40? Dossier 1 has no facility ban and hate-crime law but assessment says "among harshest." I'll set 1 = 0.41, 4 = 0.47.
